To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of Co/Al-LDs and Ni/Al-LDs into LDPE matrix led to the formation of a new high temperature polymer crystalline domain.
The rheological behavior of the LDPE/layered double hydroxides (LDH) nanocomposites was influenced by the nature of the intercalated anion and the type of metal cation in the LDH.
The addition of hydrophobic LDH to LDPE promoted the formation of a new crystalline phase, and the rheological behavior was dependent on the nature of the anions and metal cations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials based on LDPE filled with hydrophobized LDH.
the influence of the nature of the intercalated anions and of the metal in the LDH on the rheological properties of the LDPE/LDH nanocomposites.
the development of new polymeric materials with improved rheological properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rheological properties of LDPE filled with hydrophobized LDH are influenced by the nature of the intercalant anion, and that the interaction between the filler and the polymer is more important than the filler concentration.
the presence of hydrophobic LDHs in LDPE matrix, in general, promotes phase separation and reduction in shear modulus.
the rheological behavior of the LDPE filled with hydrophobized LDH depends on the type of metal cation, the anion and the amount of LDH filler.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Co/Al-LDsH and Ni/Al-LDs have different effects on the rheological properties of LDPE.
the rheology properties of LDPE filled with hydrophobized Co/Al and Ni/Al-LDHS are influenced by their chemical nature and the interaction of the filler with the polymer matrix.
the LDHs were not effective as nucleating agents for LDPE, but the rheological behavior of LDPE was affected by the interaction of the filler with the matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LDHs can be used to improve the mechanical properties of polyethylene.
the rheological properties of the LDPE/Co/Al and Ni/Al-LDHS composites are dependent on the anionic surfactants used in the intercalation process of these layered materials.
LDPE filled with hydrophobized Ni/Al-LDHS can be used as an alternative to conventional fillers for the production of plastic materials.
